subject: Hosted API public terms — simplify data transfer & subprocessor lines
messages:
From: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@horizonai.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@horizonai.com
Date: Tue, 07 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API language — quick public snippet request

Hi Jonas,

Quick ask from our security and procurement teams — we're updating Horizon's vendor security one-pager and would like a very short, plain-language blurb (1–2 sentences) we can put under a "How your data is handled" callout that links to your DPA. The engineering team found the current console copy a bit technical (mentions "subprocessors" and "transfer safeguards") and our procurement reviewers asked for wording that customers can digest quickly.

Specific constraints:
- 1–2 short sentences for our public facing one-pager
- A second, slightly longer sentence (optional) that can go in a tooltip in your Console (max ~220 chars)
- Can reference things like SOC 2 or standard safeguards but avoid legalese such as "data processor"/"controller" in the short blurb

We have a deadline for Friday (6/11) to finalize the doc for an executive review. Can you point us to an approved snippet or propose two alternatives we can choose between? Attaching a screenshot of current console text for context.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Thompson
Head of Platform Partnerships, Horizon AI
Sara.Thompson@horizonai.com

Attachment: screenshot-current-console-copy.png

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@horizonai.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API language — quick public snippet request

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear brief and the screenshot. Looping in Kim (privacy/legal liaison) and Laura (developer docs) for conservative wording and Console constraints.

Below are two short options we use internally; I added a slightly longer tooltip candidate after each. Please tell us which direction feels clearer to your reviewers and we'll fast-track a final approved version.

Option A (plain, focuses on transfers):
- Short snippet (1 line): "We may transfer data to trusted service providers and operate under standard international safeguards — see our DPA for details."
- Tooltip (~200 chars): "Redwood uses vetted service providers across regions and implements industry-standard protections (e.g., encryption, contractual safeguards). See DPA for the full list of subprocessors and transfer measures."

Option B (privacy-first, minimal jargon):
- Short snippet (1 line): "We only share data with vetted partners and protect it with industry-standard safeguards — see our DPA for details."
- Tooltip (~180 chars): "Redwood works with a limited set of third-party partners and keeps security controls and contractual safeguards in place when data moves between regions. See DPA for the partner list."

Notes for your team:
- We intentionally avoid the word "subprocessor" in the short line and use "service providers" or "partners" for customer-facing copy.
- If you need an explicit callout to SOC 2, we can append "(SOC 2 Type II)" to the tooltip.

I'll leave the legal-level finalization to Kim/Laura, but wanted to give these quick options so you can meet your Friday deadline.

Jonas Weber
Head of Developer Relations, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachment: public-terms-snippets-v1.txt

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@horizonai.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jun 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API language — quick public snippet request

Forwarding with edits — I tightened Option B and suggested placement guidance for Console UX. Edits are minor but important for accuracy and auditability. See attached v2.

Edited Option B (final suggestion):
- Short snippet (customer-facing, ~1 line): "We only share data with a small set of vetted partners and protect it with industry-standard measures — see our DPA for details."
- Tooltip (Console, ~200 chars): "Redwood works with a limited set of vetted partners and uses contractual and technical safeguards when data is processed or moved across regions (SOC 2 Type II audited). See DPA for partner list and transfer details."

Placement guidance for Console:
- Keep short snippet on the public-facing summary card (max 120 characters displayed; we recommend truncation behavior so it never wraps more than two lines).
- Tooltip should contain the mention of SOC 2 and link to a dedicated DPA page. Avoid listing subprocessors inline in the tooltip — instead use a link to an expandable subpage that lists names and locations.

Legal/accuracy notes:
- "Partners" is customer-friendly; legal teams still may request the parenthetical "(subprocessors/service providers)" elsewhere in the DPA but keep customer-facing UI copy simple.
- We should provide a stable link to the DPA and a timestamp for the subprocessor list (e.g., "subprocessors as of 2027-06-01") to help procurement teams reconcile changes.

I've attached public-terms-snippets-v2.txt with the copy in plain text and a short rationale for each edit. If Horizon needs DocuSign for a DPA amendment, route that to contracts@redwood.com; we can prioritize.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachment: public-terms-snippets-v2.txt

From: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@horizonai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, contracts@horizonai.com
Date: Thu, 09 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API language — quick public snippet request

Kim/Jonas — this is great, thank you. Horizon's procurement and legal teams reviewed both options and prefer your "Edited Option B" as-is, with a single small tweak: please change "a small set" to "a limited set" (our reviewers felt "small" could be interpreted as "too few partners" whereas "limited" signals curation).

If you can provide the final one-line snippet and tooltip text with that tweak, we'll slot it into the one-pager and link to the DPA. Also asking our legal ops to confirm whether they need a DPA amendment or just a pointer to the existing DPA page — contracts@horizonai.com will follow up if they need DocuSign.

Final tweak request (exact text we will use):
- Short snippet: "We only share data with a limited set of vetted partners and protect it with industry-standard measures — see our DPA for details."
- Tooltip: "Redwood works with a limited set of vetted partners and uses contractual and technical safeguards when data is processed or moved across regions (SOC 2 Type II audited). See DPA for partner list and transfer details."

If you can confirm by EOD tomorrow (6/10) we'll hit our Friday deadline.

Best,
Sara Thompson
Head of Platform Partnerships, Horizon AI
